## 3\. An exact adversarial obstruction to simply increasing shear strength

There is also a useful exact calculation showing why the three-shear low-block result cannot be extended to arbitrarily large Fourier cutoffs merely by increasing \(s\)\.

Consider the initial complex Fourier mode

\[
u_0(x)=e_3 e^{2\pi ix_1}.
\]

Taking its real part gives a smooth real divergence-free initial field.

Under the first actuator \((p,a)=(e_1,e_2)\), this mode is invariant for every admissible calibration: its wavevector is parallel to the actuator frequency, while every actual polarization remains perpendicular to that frequency.

For the second actuator \((e_2,e_3)\), take

\[
\theta_2=1,\qquad\phi_2=0,\qquad
e^{\rm cal}_2=\frac{1}{2\pi s_2}e_1.
\]

For every \(s_2\ge1024\), this error is smaller than \(\rho_0\)\.

The exact velocity Leray evolution remains polarized along \(e_3\), so the second shear reduces to an exact scalar advection calculation\:

\[
U_2(s_2)u_0
=
e_3e^{2\pi ix_1}
e^{i\cos(2\pi x_2)}.
\]

Its Fourier coefficient at

\[
q=(1,1024,0)
\]

is

\[
\widehat u(q)=i^{1024}J_{1024}(1)e_3
=J_{1024}(1)e_3.
\]

The Bessel coefficient is strictly positive. In fact,

\[
J_{1024}(1)
\ge
\frac{1-\frac1{4(1025)}}{2^{1024}1024!}>0.
\]

For the third actuator \((e_3,e_1)\), choose

\[
\theta_3=1,\qquad\phi_3=0,\qquad
e^{\rm cal}_3=-\frac1{1024}e_2.
\]

This error is admissible, with norm exactly \(\rho_0\)\. At the selected Fourier mode,

\[
\left(e_1-\frac1{1024}e_2\right)\cdot(1,1024,0)=0.
\]

Therefore the third actuator leaves this Fourier coefficient unchanged, regardless of its integrated pulse strength. Since it preserves the first two Fourier coordinates, other second-stage modes cannot contribute to this particular output coefficient either.

Consequently,

\[
\boxed{
\left|
\widehat{
U_3(s_3)U_2(s_2)U_1(s_1)u_0
}(1,1024,0)
\right|
=J_{1024}(1)>0
}
\tag{11}
\]

for the specified admissible calibrations, every \(s_1,s_3\), and every \(s_2\ge1024\)\.

This demonstrates something stronger than the earlier informal concern about resonances: **arbitrarily strong versions of this particular three-pulse word retain a nonzero calibrated high-frequency return channel**\.
